assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions neurons (cells) in the brain but does not address the unicellular vs multicellular distinction or give examples like bacteria vs humans. It is only tangentially about cells.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses neurons and brain function but does not describe levels of biological organization from cells to biosphere, nor does it use a labeled diagram. It is not direct support for this competency.

copy.en:
How many neurons are in your brain?

About 86 billion! They're connected in so many ways, which is how your brain can learn, think, and store memories.
copy.tl:
Ilang neuron mayroon ang utak mo?

Humigit-kumulang na 86 bilyon! Konektado ang mga ito sa napakaraming paraan, kaya kaya ng utak mong matuto, mag-isip, at mag-imbak ng alaala.
copy.bis:
Pila ka neuron ang naa sa imong utok?

Mga 86 ka bilyon! Nagkonektar kini sa daghan kaayong paagi, mao nga makahimo ang imong utok sa pagkat-on, paghunahuna, ug pagtipig og handumanan.

copy.en: The brain is the body's control center — it's where thinking, memory, and feelings happen, and it sends commands to the rest of the body.
copy.tl: Ang utak ang sentro ng kontrol ng katawan — dito nangyayari ang pag-iisip, alaala, at damdamin, at dito rin nanggagaling ang mga utos sa ibang bahagi ng katawan.
copy.bis: Ang utok mao ang sentro sa pagdumala sa lawas — dinhi mahitabo ang panghuna-huna, handumanan, ug pagbati, ug gikan dinhi mopadala og sugo ngadto sa ubang bahin sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your brain has three main parts: the cerebrum for thinking and movement, the cerebellum for balance, and the brainstem for automatic jobs like breathing.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the brain, which is part of the nervous system, not any of the systems listed in G4-L-1 (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It shares the broad topic of human body systems but does not directly support the specified competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your brain has three main parts: the cerebrum for thinking and movement, the cerebellum for balance, and the brainstem for automatic jobs like breathing.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the three main parts of the brain and their functions, but it does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together. It is only related to the nervous system, not the integration of systems as required by G8-L-2.

copy.en: Your brain has three main parts: the cerebrum for thinking and movement, the cerebellum for balance, and the brainstem for automatic jobs like breathing.
copy.tl: May tatlong pangunahing bahagi ang utak: ang cerebrum para sa pag-iisip at kilos, ang cerebellum para sa balanse, at ang brainstem para sa awtomatikong gawain gaya ng paghinga.
copy.bis: Adunay tulo ka nag-unang bahin ang utok: ang cerebrum para sa panghunahuna ug paglihok, ang cerebellum para sa balanse, ug ang brainstem para sa awtomatik nga buluhaton sama sa pagginhawa.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the brain but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. Helmet safety is injury prevention, not instruction on body system function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wearing a helmet when biking helps protect your brain if you fall or crash!

A bicycle helmet is not one of the listed vehicle safety measures and the card does not gather information from secondary sources.

copy.en: Wearing a helmet when biking helps protect your brain if you fall or crash!
copy.tl: Ang pagsuot ng helmet kapag nagbibisikleta ay tumutulong maprotektahan ang utak kapag nadapa o nabangga!
copy.bis: Ang pagsul-ob og helmet kung magbisikleta makatabang sa pagpanalipod sa utok kung mahulog o mabangga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The brain's left half controls the right side of the body, and the right half controls the left.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The brain's left half controls the right side of the body, and the right half controls the left.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: G8-L-2 requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The card is a simple factual statement about brain control of body sides, uses no model or diagram, and does not explain how any body systems work together. It is only tangentially related to body systems.

copy.en:
Which side of your brain controls your right hand?

Surprisingly, the left side! The brain's left half controls the right side of the body, and the right half controls the left.
copy.tl:
Aling bahagi ng utak ang kumokontrol sa kanang kamay?

Ang kaliwang panig pala! Kontrolado ng kaliwang panig ng utak ang kanang bahagi ng katawan, at ang kanang panig naman ang sa kaliwa.
copy.bis:
Unsang kilid sa utok ang nagkontrol sa tuong kamot?

Ang walang kilid diay! Ang walang kilid sa utok magkontrol sa tuong bahin sa lawas, ug ang tuong kilid magkontrol sa wala.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When you stop exercising, your breathing doesn't stay fast — it slowly returns to normal.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses breathing rate returning to normal after exercise, but does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work, which is the focus of G5-L-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When you stop exercising, your breathing doesn't stay fast — it slowly returns to normal.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a physiological adjustment after exercise, but does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or mention its indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure). It only touches on a related concept without directly supporting the competency.

copy.en: When you stop exercising, your breathing doesn't stay fast — it slowly returns to normal.
copy.tl: Kapag tumigil ka sa pag-eehersisyo, unti-unting bumabagal ang iyong paghinga hanggang sa bumalik ito sa dati.
copy.bis: Kon mohunong ka sa pag-ehersisyo, hinay-hinay nga mobalik sa naandan ang imong pagginhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The top of each cantilever is under tension, while the bottom is under compression.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes tension and compression in a bridge structure, but it does not address how forces change the shape of objects through pushing, pulling, stretching, bending, twisting, or squeezing. It shares force-related vocabulary but gives no direct instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They project outward from their supports! The top of each cantilever is under tension, while the bottom is under compression.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a structural situation involving tension and compression, but it does not identify or describe balanced or unbalanced forces, nor does it use examples such as a resting box, standing man, constant velocity, falling fruit, or accelerating car. It is only broadly related to forces.

copy.en:
How do the sections of a cantilever bridge stick out?

They project outward from their supports! The top of each cantilever is under tension, while the bottom is under compression.
copy.tl:
Paano lumalabas ang mga bahagi ng isang cantilever bridge?

Lumalagpas sila papalayo mula sa suporta! Ang itaas ng cantilever ay nasa tension, at ang ibaba ay nasa compression.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsalig sa gawas ang mga seksyon sa cantilever bridge?

Nagsalig sila sa gawas gikan sa ilang suporta! Ang ibabaw sa cantilever naa sa tension, ug ang ubos naa sa compression.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is a famous cantilever bridge made of strong steel and concrete.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a bridge as a structure but does not explain its impact on everyday life, nor does it use information from home or the local community to do so. It only states the bridge type and materials.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is a famous cantilever bridge made of strong steel and concrete.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects, activities, or natural events observed in their local environment that can be explained by science
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a bridge, which is an object that can be explained by science, but it does not identify it as an object/activity/event explained by science or connect it to the local environment in a way that supports the competency's skill of identifying such phenomena.

copy.en:
What kind of bridge connects Cebu City and Mactan Island?

The Mactan-Mandaue Bridge! It is a famous cantilever bridge made of strong steel and concrete.
copy.tl:
Anong uri ng tulay ang nag-uugnay sa Cebu City at Mactan Island?

Ang Mactan-Mandaue Bridge! Ito ay isang sikat na cantilever bridge na gawa sa matibay na steel at concrete.
copy.bis:
Unsang klase nga tulay ang nag-ugnay sa Cebu City ug Mactan Island?

Ang Mactan-Mandaue Bridge! Kini usa ka bantog nga cantilever bridge nga gihimo sa lig-on nga steel ug concrete.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a fracture, which is a condition of the skeletal system, but it does not describe how the skeletal system works. It provides no information about the function, structure, or operation of the skeletal system as required by the competency.

copy.en: A fracture is simply a break or crack in a bone.
copy.tl: Ang fracture ay isang bali o lamat sa buto.
copy.bis: Ang fracture mao ang bali o liki sa bukog.

copy.en: Bronze was one of the very first alloys people made, which is why we have the Bronze Age in history!
copy.tl: Ang bronse ay isa sa mga pinakaunang aleasyon na ginawa ng tao, kaya may Panahon ng Bronse sa kasaysayan!
copy.bis: Ang bronse usa sa mga unang aleasyon nga gihimo sa tawo, mao nga adunay Panahon sa Bronse sa kasaysayan!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria, which are unicellular organisms, but it does not teach the concept of unicellular vs. multicellular organisms. It only uses the word 'bacteria' in the context of tooth decay, providing no direct instructional support for recognizing that some organisms are single-celled and others are multi-celled.

copy.en: Brushing your teeth twice a day removes leftover food and bacteria that cause tooth decay.
copy.tl: Ang pagsisipilyo ng ngipin nang dalawang beses sa isang araw ay nag-aalis ng natitirang pagkain at bacteria na sanhi ng pagkabulok ng ngipin.
copy.bis: Ang pagsipilyo sa ngipon kaduha sa usa ka adlaw mokuha sa nahabilin nga pagkaon ug bacteria nga hinungdan sa pagkabulok sa ngipon.

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe chemical properties of materials such as burning, reacting, or being degradable/biodegradable. It concerns food contamination and can safety, which is not the intended chemical-properties content.

copy.en: Never eat from a can that's bulging, rusty, or leaking — it could be holding dangerous bacteria inside.
copy.tl: Huwag kainin ang laman ng latang bukol (bulging), kalawang, o tumutulo — baka may nakakalasong bakterya ito.
copy.bis: Ayaw kan-a ang sulod sa lata nga burot, taya, o nagtulo — basin naay makahilo nga bakterya niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: These air-filled floats keep the boat on the water surface and maintain perfect balance!

copy.en: The Filipino bangka has outriggers, called katig, on both sides to prevent capsizing. These air-filled floats keep the boat on the water surface and maintain perfect balance!
copy.tl: Ang bangkang Pilipino ay may mga katig (outrigger) sa magkabilang panig para hindi bumaligtad. Ang mga air-filled float na ito ay nagpapanatili sa bangka sa ibabaw ng tubig at nagba-balance!
copy.bis: Ang bangkang Pilipino adunay mga katig (outrigger) sa duha ka kilid aron dili matalsik. Kining mga air-filled float nagpadayon sa bangka sa ibabaw sa tubig ug nagbalanse!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions density, which relates to heaviness, but it does not explore or describe how size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture affect the movement of objects. It only states a single fact about helium balloon buoyancy.

copy.en: A helium balloon floats because helium is less dense than the surrounding air! Buoyancy works in the air, not just in water.
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang helium balloon dahil ang helium ay mas mababang densidad kaysa sa hangin! Ang buoyancy ay gumagana sa hangin, hindi lang sa tubig.
copy.bis: Mulutang ang helium balloon tungod kay ang helium mas ubos nga densidad kaysa sa hangin! Ang buoyancy molihok sa hangin, dili lang sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oil floats on top of water because it is lighter, or less dense, than water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains density and floating but does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oil floats on top of water because it is lighter, or less dense, than water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a liquid (oil and water) but does not describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. Density is not the same as the shape/volume properties targeted by this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oil floats on top of water because it is lighter, or less dense, than water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: This competency is about factors affecting the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). The card is about density and floating, not about movement of objects or the listed factors. No direct or prerequisite support.

copy.en:
Why does oil always float on top of water?

Oil floats on top of water because it is lighter, or less dense, than water!
copy.tl:
Bakit laging lumulutang ang langis sa ibabaw ng tubig?

Lumulutang ang langis sa ibabaw ng tubig dahil mas magaan o mas mababa ang densidad nito kaysa sa tubig.
copy.bis:
Nganong kanunay nga nagalutaw ang lana sa ibabaw sa tubig?

Nagalutaw ang lana sa ibabaw sa tubig kay mas gaan o mas ubos ang densidad niini kaysa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It sinks when it fills its tanks with water, and rises when it pushes the water out with air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water (liquid) and air (gas) but does not teach that matter exists in three states (solid, liquid, gas). It explains buoyancy via ballast tanks, not the states of matter concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It sinks when it fills its tanks with water, and rises when it pushes the water out with air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects at home and in the classroom as solid, liquid or gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not ask students to identify objects at home or in the classroom as solid, liquid, or gas. It only incidentally names water and air while explaining submarine operation, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
How does a submarine sink and rise?

It sinks when it fills its tanks with water, and rises when it pushes the water out with air!
copy.tl:
Paano lumulubog at lumulutang ang isang submarino?

Lumulubog ito kapag pinuno ng tubig ang mga tangke nito, at lumulutang kapag pinalayas ang tubig gamit ang hangin!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsalud ug paglutaw sa submarino?

Maunlod kini kon pun-on og tubig ang mga tangke, ug molutaw kon itulod ang tubig pagawas gamit ang hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A burnay isn't just for decoration! It is a super useful tool we use every day to store food, water, and yummy vinegar.

assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies burnay as a useful item for storage, but it does not describe what natural materials (e.g., clay) were used to make it. The competency requires both identifying useful things made from non-living materials and describing the natural materials used. The card only covers the usefulness aspect, not the material composition, so it does not directly support the full competency.

copy.en: A burnay isn't just for decoration! It is a super useful tool we use every day to store food, water, and yummy vinegar.
copy.tl: Hindi lang palamuti ang burnay! Ito ay tunay na kasangkapan na ginagamit araw-araw para mag-imbak ng pagkain, tubig, at masarap na suka.
copy.bis: Dili lang dekorasyon ang burnay! Kini tinuod nga kasangkapan nga gigamit adlaw-adlaw aron tipigan ang pagkaon, tubig, ug lami nga suka.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When wood burns, matter is not destroyed!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that chemical equations demonstrate a rearrangement of atoms but the total mass of the system remains the same during a chemical reaction
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that matter is not destroyed during burning, which touches on conservation of mass, but it does not mention chemical equations, rearrangement of atoms, or the total mass of the system remaining the same. It only gives a qualitative explanation of why ash is lighter, without connecting to the specific competency content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When wood burns, matter is not destroyed!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: apply the principles of conservation of mass to balance chemical equations
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates the principle of conservation of mass in a burning reaction, but it does not apply the principle to balancing chemical equations. There is no equation, no balancing, and no quantitative treatment, so it does not directly support the skill of balancing equations.

copy.en:
Why is leftover ash so much lighter than the original wood?

When wood burns, matter is not destroyed! Most of it turns into gas and smoke that float into the air, leaving the ash much lighter.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas magaan ang naiiwang abo kaysa sa orihinal na kahoy?

Kapag nasusunog ang kahoy, hindi nawawala ang matter! Karamihan nito ay nagiging gas at usok na lumilipad sa hangin, kaya ang naiiwang abo ay magaan lang.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas gaan ang nahabilin nga abo kay sa orihinal nga kahoy?

Kung masunog ang kahoy, dili mawala ang matter! Kadaghanan niini mahimong gas ug aso nga molupad sa hangin, mao nga gaan ra ang nahabilin nga abo.

Can you eat too much calcium?

Calcium is good, but no need to overdo it — the body only takes what it needs and removes the rest. Just eat the right amount each day.

Pwede bang sumobra sa pag-inom ng calcium?

Mabuti ang calcium, pero hindi kailangang sumobra — kumukuha lang ang katawan ng kailangan at inaalis ang sobra. Sapat lang araw-araw.
copy.bis:
Mahimo ba nga mosobra sa pagkaon og calcium?

Maayo ang calcium, apan dili kinahanglan mosobra — mokuha ra ang lawas sa gikinahanglan ug i-tangtang ang sobra. Sakto ra kada adlaw.

Does more calcium make bones stronger faster?

No! Your body only needs the right amount of calcium—extra isn't used and can even cause problems. A balanced diet is best.

Mas lumalakas ba agad ang buto kapag maraming calcium?

Hindi! Tama lang ang kailangan ng katawan sa calcium—ang sobra ay hindi nagagamit at maaari pang makasama. Mas mainam ang balanseng pagkain.
copy.bis:
Molig-on ba dayon ang bukog kung daghan og calcium?

Dili! Sakto ra ang gikinahanglan sa lawas nga calcium—ang sobra dili magamit ug makadaot pa. Mas maayo ang balanse nga pagkaon.

copy.bis: Ang husto nga gitas-on sa pabilo naghimo og perpekto nga kalayo! Kung sobra taas, aso; kung mubo, gamay. Pagtupad niini aron limpyo ang pagsiga.

copy.en:
How does water rise against gravity inside a sponge?

When a sponge touches water, it rises through tiny holes via capillary action! Adhesion to the material and cohesion between water molecules pull the water upward.
copy.tl:
Paano umaahon ang tubig laban sa gravity sa loob ng isang espongha?

Kapag nahawakan ng espongha ang tubig, umaahon ito sa mga maliit na butas sa pamamagitan ng capillary action! Ang adhesion sa materyales at cohesion ng mga molekula ay nagpupuwersa ng tubig pataas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsaka sa tubig batok sa gravity sulod sa espongha?

Sa paghikap sa espongha sa tubig, motaas kini pinaagi sa gagmayng mga butas tungod sa capillary action! Ang adhesion sa materyal ug cohesion sa mga molekula nagkuha sa tubig pataas.

copy.en:
Do all liquids climb up tubes?

Nope! Mercury actually sinks lower in a narrow tube because its cohesion is stronger than its adhesion to glass.
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng likido ay umaakyat sa tubo?

Hindi! Bumababa pa ang merkuryo sa makitid na tubo dahil mas malakas ang cohesion nito kaysa adhesion sa salamin.
copy.bis:
Tanang likido ba mosaka sa tubo?

Dili! Monaog pa ang merkuryo sa pig-ot nga tubo tungod kay mas kusog ang cohesion niini kaysa adhesion sa bildo.

How does a car engine make the wheels turn?

It burns gasoline inside tiny chambers! Those mini explosions push pistons up and down super fast, and that motion turns the wheels.
copy.tl:

Nagsusunog ito ng gasolina sa loob ng maliliit na silid! Ang maliliit na pagsabog na iyon ay nagtutulak sa mga piston pataas at pababa nang mabilis, at ang galaw na iyon ang pumapaikot sa mga gulong.

Nagasunog kini og gasolina sulod sa gagmay nga mga kwarto! Kining gagmay nga mga pagbuto motulod sa mga piston pataas ug paubos nga paspas, ug kana nga lihok mopapadagan sa mga ligid.

A cool carabao stays healthier, works stronger, and makes more milk — like the milk used for kesong puti — so its mud bath really matters!
copy.tl:
Bakit mahalagang panatilihing malamig ang kalabaw?

Ang malamig na kalabaw ay mas malusog, mas malakas magtrabaho, at mas marami ang gatas na ibinibigay, gaya ng ginagamit sa kesong puti — kaya mahalaga ang paglublob nito!
copy.bis:
Nganong importante nga bugnawon ang kalabaw?

Ang bugnaw nga kalabaw mas himsog, mas kusgan motrabaho, ug mas daghan og gatas nga mahatag, sama sa gigamit sa kesong puti — mao nga importante ang paglunang niini!
